findings.text: nothing in the repository guards lockfile freshness: no CI workflow, no test referencing uv.lock or uv lock --check, and no pre-commit lock check, so a pyproject edit that leaves uv.lock stale (the exact defect this node repaired, already committed once by the member node) is not caught automatically; the repo's uv shim forces --no-sync on every uv run, so an ordinary run neither heals nor reports the staleness.

the fragment sets plan-verifies cocos-standalone-distribution#s1, but this node verifies only the lock-coherence portion of s1's compound done-when; the wheel METADATA, clean py3.12 venv install, re-export identity, five COCOS test modules and imas-ambix resolve were verified (or not) on the member node, so a reader following plan-verifies to this fragment alone would over-credit s1.

item_verdicts.call_sites: a lockfile is a build artifact with no code call sites; the member graph it resolves is consumed by uv, and the package it names (nova_cocos) is imported by nova's COCOS modules and the imas-ambix checkout recorded on the member node.
item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against b85115a12; 4b3d1a90f adds the member to manifest.members, adds the [[package]] nova-cocos block and adds the nova-cocos entry to nova-stella's dependencies and requires-dist, and 8876ea26 adds only the evidence fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: the node's own gate is uv lock --check (EXIT=0) plus a before/after package comparison; both reproduce; the node makes no claim about s1's wheel-build, clean-py3.12-venv, re-export-identity, COCOS-test or imas-ambix-resolve elements, which belong to the member node.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is to regenerate uv.lock so the nova-cocos workspace member declared at b85115a12 resolves; the +10-line uv.lock change lands it, verified by uv lock --check EXIT=0 at the head.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it states uv lock --check EXIT=0 and uv lock EXIT=0, records the +10/-0 lock diff, the editable member source, the gained dependency entries and the ADDED=[nova-cocos]/REMOVED=[]/VERSION-CHANGED=[] comparison, and names its two log paths.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the declared paths and git diff --name-status: every changed path is inside the declared set, nothing extra.

justifications.durability: the repaired defect is caught by uv lock --check, which genuinely fails on a stale lock (reviewer arm EXIT=1 at base), but nothing in the repository runs it: there is no .github/workflows and no .gitlab-ci.yml, no test references uv.lock or "uv lock --check", and scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit performs only the filepath-relativize check; the same staleness recurred once already (the member node edited pyproject and left the lock behind) and the repo's uv shim forces --no-sync on every uv run, so an ordinary run neither heals nor reports a stale lock.
justifications.evidence: two standalone gate logs exist and both reproduce: uv-lock.log (uv lock resolution, EXIT=0, 288 packages, "Added nova-cocos (dynamic)") and version-compare.log (before 287 -> after 288, ADDED=[nova-cocos], REMOVED=[], VERSION-CHANGED=[]); the reviewer independently re-ran uv lock --check in extracted base and head trees (base EXIT=1 "The lockfile at uv.lock needs to be updated", head EXIT=0 "Resolved 288 packages in 3ms") and re-derived the package diff with tomllib, matching the node's version-compare.log exactly; the deduction is that the node never read the plan HTML (its own manifest records a storage-slow read_plan and reconstructs s1 from pyproject.toml plus the sibling fragment), and the version-comparison is a worker-authored script rather than an independent tool, though it reproduces trivially.
justifications.fit: uv.lock is in the canonical machine-generated form uv itself emits, and the new evidence fragment matches its sibling ncsd-nova-cocos-member.html in every meta field, section id and table id, so it renders and lists under the same conventions.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the node's goal is to regenerate uv.lock so the nova-cocos workspace member resolves coherently; at head 8876ea26 uv.lock carries manifest.members=[nova-cocos,nova-stella], a [[package]] nova-cocos block with source={editable="packages/nova-cocos"}, and the nova-cocos reference in nova-stella's dependencies and requires-dist, which is exactly the member graph the root pyproject at b85115a12 declares but the lock did not carry.
justifications.reuse: no duplication is introduced: the change adds only the member reference uv computes from the already-declared workspace, leaving the single canonical lockfile in place and forking no resolver or version source.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-status b85115a12 8876ea26 lists exactly M uv.lock and A docs/evidence/fragments/cocos-standalone-distribution/ncsd-nova-cocos-lock.html, both inside the node's declared write paths [uv.lock, docs/evidence/fragments/cocos-standalone-distribution/ncsd-nova-cocos-lock.html, docs/figures/cocos-standalone-distribution/ncsd-nova-cocos-lock]; the declared figures directory was unused, which is not a defect; commit messages are conventional with bodies and carry no attribution trailer.
